subject: human cells
title: The 5 Longest-Living Cells in Your Body, Ranked (#1 Is as Old as You)

scenes.text: The five longest-living cells in your body, ranked. Most of you is under ten years old.

scenes.label: Gut lining · 5 days
scenes.text: Number five: the lining of your gut. About five days, then it's gone. Your food is tougher than it is.

scenes.label: Skin · 2 weeks
scenes.text: Number four: skin. The surface renews itself roughly every two weeks. The face you had last month is dust.

scenes.label: Red blood cells · 4 months
scenes.text: Number three: red blood cells. Around four months. Then your body breaks them down and recycles the iron.

scenes.label: Fat cells · 10 years
scenes.text: Number two: fat cells. About ten percent die and get replaced each year, so each one lasts roughly a decade.

scenes.label: Brain neurons · your whole life
scenes.text: Number one: the neurons in your cerebral cortex. Carbon dating shows they're as old as you are. Never replaced. So yes, as old as you.

description:
The five longest-living cells in your body, ranked by average lifespan.
Karolinska Institute researchers used carbon-14 from Cold War bomb tests to date human cells: gut lining about 5 days, skin about 2 weeks, red blood cells about 4 months, fat cells about 10 years, and cortical neurons as old as the person, never replaced.
Which number surprised you most?
first_comment: Which one would you have put at number one? And what should we rank next: the fastest things in your body, or the heaviest?
